rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening resumes the preceding rebuke: the deniers reject and deem impossible the resurrection that the Prophet calls them to believe in.
rows.anchor: استئناف لتقرير ما قبله من زجرهم عن اتباعه عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first أنكم may be construed with an implicit preposition (بأنكم), though the preposition may also be unexpressed.
rows.anchor: على تقدير حرف الجر أي بأنكم ويجوز أن لا يقدر نحو وعدتك الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard kasra on mīm follows مات يمات; another reading has ḍamma, following مات يموت.
rows.anchor: بكسر الميم من مات يمات وقريء بضمها من مات يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that former flesh and similar parts become dust, while others become bare, decayed bones; dust comes first because its transformation is especially implausible and it derives from visible parts.
rows.anchor: وكان بعض أجزائكم من اللحم ونظائره ترابا وبعضها عظاما نخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, earlier generations were wholly dust, while later generations are bones.
rows.anchor: أو وكان متقدموكم ترابا صرفا ومتأخروكم عظاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second أنكم reinforces the first after the long separation from its predicate مخرجون.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لأنكم الأول ولطول الفصل بينه وبين خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised outcome is that they will emerge alive from their graves as before, after dying and becoming dust.
rows.anchor: أي أيعدكم أنكم مخرجون من قبوركم أحياء كما كنتم أولا

rows.speaker: الفراء والجرمي والمبرد
rows.claim: They attach إذا to مخرجون; this does not mean emergence occurs at the instant of death, despite Abu Nizar's objection, which al-Sakhawi refutes and al-Suyuti transmits.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا الإعراب الفراء والجرمي والمبرد ولا يلزم من ذلك كون الإخراج وقت الموت

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh treats the second أنكم as an emphatic بدل of the first; the first predicate is omitted, inferred from the second, and governs إذا. An adverb of time cannot directly predicate of a person unless إخراجكم is understood.
rows.anchor: وفيه معنى التأكيد وخبر أن الأولى محذوف لدلالة خبر الثانية عليه

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad objects to Sibawayh's بدل analysis because it lacks an independent constituent: the first أن has no stated predicate.
rows.anchor: وكان المبرد يأبى البدل لكونه من غير مستقل إذ لم يذكر خبر أن الأولى

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash derives مخرجون from an omitted يحدث: either the conditional clause predicates the first أن and the omitted verb answers إذا, or that verb is the predicate and governs إذا; another attribution makes أنكم مخرجون the subject of إذا.
rows.anchor: وذهب الأخفش إلى أن ( أنكم مخرجون ) مقدر بمصدر مرفوع بفعل محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parsing makes أنكم مخرجون the subject and إذا متم its predicate, with the clause serving as predicate of the first أن; al-Baḥr calls this easy, and al-Sakhawi attributes it to al-Mubarrad.
rows.anchor: أن يكون ( أنكم مخرجون ) مبتدأ و ( إذا متم ) خبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the parsing reported from al-Farra and his associates as best suited to the Qur'anic word order.
rows.anchor: والذي يقتضيه جزالة النظم الكريم ما ذكرناه عن الفراء ومن معه

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah omits the first أنكم and reads أيعدكم إذا متم.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( أيعدكم إذا متم ) بإسقاط ( أنكم ) الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying wording is إن الحياة إلا حياتنا الدنيا; the pronoun replaces الحياة because the predicate identifies it, a permitted backward reference when the predicate explains its antecedent.
rows.anchor: أصله إن الحياة إلا حياتنا الدنيا ثم وضع الضمير موضع الحياة لأن الخبر يدل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection notes that the predicate is qualified, so including that qualification in the pronoun's antecedent would make the sentence tautological; the response is that a pronoun may refer to the noun without its qualification.
rows.anchor: واعترض بأن الخبر موصوف فتلاحظ الصفة في ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi's preferred explanation is that the pronoun refers to the mentally understood genus of life, yielding their intended denial: no life exists except worldly life.
rows.anchor: بأن الضمير عائد على ما يفهم من جنس الحياة ليفيد الحمل ما قصدوه من نفي البعث

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the pronoun refers to a mentally familiar concept signaled by what follows, as in هذا أخوك, rather than repeating the predicate as its antecedent.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف ليس المعنى النفس النفس لأنه لا يصلح الثاني حينئذ تفسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion illustrates backward reference with the expression هي العرب تقول ما شاءت and the line هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل وللدهر أيام تجوز وتعدل.
rows.anchor: وللدهر أيام تجوز وتعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains their claim that life is only worldly: some die and others are born in turn, not that individuals live again after death, which would contradict their denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: جملة مفسرة لما ادعوه من أن الحياة هي الحياة الدنيا وأرادوا بذلك يموت بعضنا ويولد بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed senses are death as nonexistence before birth, or the children's survival counting as their parents' continued life; al-Alusi considers these explanations far-fetched.
rows.anchor: أرادوا بالموت العدم السابق على الوجود أو أرادوا بالحياة بقاء أولادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further proposal is that they believed in transmigration: a departed soul successively enters newly formed bodies; al-Alusi says he does not regard this proposal as far-fetched.
rows.anchor: أن القوم كانوا قائلين بالتناسخ فحياتهم بتعلق النفس التي فارقت أبدانهم بأبدان أخر عنصرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed sequence may resemble one reading of Jesus' words in 3:55: conjunction with wāw does not require chronological order, so their intended life could precede death.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى لعيسى عليه السلام ( إني متوفيك ورافعك إلى ) على قول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may actually have said نحيا ونموت, with the order changed in the report to fit إن هي إلا حياتنا الدنيا.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنهم قالوا نحيا ونموت إلا أنه لما حكى عنهم قيل ( نموت ونحيا ) ليكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their final clause makes the denial of resurrection continuous and emphatic.
rows.anchor: ثم المراد بقولهم ( وما نحن ) الخ استمرار النفي وتأكيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that the people were Thamud, Gabriel's cry destroyed them; if they were ʿAd, this conflicts with reports that a violent wind destroyed them.
rows.anchor: أي صيحة جبريل عليه السلام صاح عليه السلام بهم فدمرهم وهذا على القول بأن القرن قوم صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To reconcile the ʿAd identification, a report says Gabriel cried out from within the wind; mentioning cry and wind separately suggests either would have sufficed to destroy them.
rows.anchor: وأجاب بأن جبريل عليه السلام صاح بهم من الريح كما روي في بعض الأحاديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, الصيحة means a terrible punishment or overwhelming torment, as in the poetic idiom that time cried out against the Barmakids.
rows.anchor: العذاب المصطلم كما في قوله : صاح الزمان بآل برمك صيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بالحق attaches to أخذ and means an established, irresistible truth, as in the verse about death's stupor arriving with truth.
rows.anchor: كما في قوله تعالى : ( وجاءت سكرة الموت بالحق )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations are that the seizure was by God's justice, or fulfilled the messenger's true warning that they would soon regret their actions.
rows.anchor: من قولك : فلان يقضي بالحق إذا كان عادلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غثاء is flood debris—withered leaves and sticks; أغثاء is an irregular plural, and the ث may be geminated, as in a line by Imruʾ al-Qays about flood debris.
rows.anchor: أي كغثاء السيل وهو ما يحمله من الورق والعيدان البالية ويجمع على أغثاء شذوذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بعدا can report their distance or function as a curse; distance is opposite nearness, while the second verbal form is used for destruction, and the noun means distance from mercy, good, salvation, or utter ruin.
rows.anchor: يحتمل الإخبار والدعاء والبعد ضد القرب والهلاك وفعلهما ككرم وفرح

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: In a curse, Sibawayh requires an omitted governor for the verbal noun; the lām identifies those cursed or declared remote and attaches to an omitted expression.
rows.anchor: ويجب حذف ناصب هذا المصدر عند سيبويه فيما إذا كان دعائيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit phrase القوم الظالمين replaces a pronoun to signal that their banishment is because of their wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع الضمير إيذانا بأن إبعادهم لظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of الحق is the truth brought by the Prophet; following their desires is literal, while the attribution is figurative.
rows.anchor: الحق الذي جاء به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجعل الإتباع حقيقيا والإسناد مجازيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another paraphrase makes the Prophet the subject: had he followed their wishes, he would have brought them shirk instead of his revealed message.
rows.anchor: وقيل مآل المعنى لو اتبع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أهواءهم فجاءهم بالشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the apparent reading, God would have ruined the world and the Resurrection begun in overwhelming anger; the supposition that the Prophet could change revelation is impossible.
rows.anchor: أي لخرب الله تعالى العالم وقامت القيامة لفرط غضبه سبحانه وهو فرض محال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second analysis takes الحق as what accords with reality about divinity and اتباع metaphorically as agreement: if shirk were true, the heavens and earth would be corrupt, as argued in 21:22.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد بالحق الأمر المطابق للواقع في شأن الألوهية والإتباع مجازا عن الموافقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An objection says this analysis does not suit the context; shirk in divinity does not entail cosmic corruption, which follows from shirk in lordship, unlike Quraysh's belief as indicated in 31:25.
rows.anchor: وهو لا يستلزم الفساد والذي يستلزمه إنما هو الشرك في الربوبية كما تزعمه الثنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A broader reading says that if truth in general conformed to their desires, the heavens and earth would lose all order; this digression aptly magnifies truth as the basis of cosmic order.
rows.anchor: لو وافق الحق مطلقا أهواءهم لخرجت السماوات والأرض عن الصلاح والانتظام بالكلية

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: A report from Abu Salih, also attributed by some to Ibn Jurayj and by al-Zamakhshari to Qatada, identifies الحق as God: if God legislated shirk to please them, He would not be God and creation would be corrupted.
rows.anchor: وقد أخرجه ابن أبي شيبة وعبد بن حميد وابن جرير وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم عن أبي صالح

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: The God-as-حق interpretation presupposes that legislating shirk is a deficiency from which God must be declared free; al-Khafaji says rational proof establishes this with no disagreement.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر ذلك الخفاجي وذكر أنه قد قام الدليل العقلي عليه وأنه لا خلاف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi defends the God-as-حق reading as contextually apt: their hatred cannot change what God reveals, and it is impossible for the Prophet to be sent with what they prefer over truth.
rows.anchor: ولعل الكلام عليه اعتراض أيضا للإشارة إلى عدم إمكان إرسال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام إليهم بخلاف ما جاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says indulging their contradictory desires would disorder the world and expose their irrationality; al-Alusi dismisses it with وهو كما ترى.
rows.anchor: لو فعل الله تعالى ما يوافق أهواءهم لاختل نظام العالم لما أن آراءهم متناقضة

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththab reads the wāw in ولو with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب ( ولو اتبع ) بضم الواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse shifts from condemning their dislike of truth to condemning their rejection of what every soul naturally wants for its own good.
rows.anchor: انتقال من تشنيعهم بكراهة الحق إلى تشنيعهم بالإعراض عما جبل عليه كل نفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Qur'an, their honor and distinction; they should have eagerly accepted their own glory, but turn away from it.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالذكر القرآن الذي هو فخرهم وشرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit ذكرهم instead of a pronoun intensifies their rebuke; the فاء makes their turning away follow from God's giving them the reminder.
rows.anchor: وفي وضع الظاهر موضع الضمير مزيد تشنيع لهم وتقريع والفاء لترتيب ما بعدها من إعراضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الحق earlier means the Qur'an, God's shift from the Prophet's pronoun to the majestic first-person plural honors the Prophet; calling it truth suits the denial context, while calling it reminder suits divine attribution.
rows.anchor: الإتيان بالذكر إلى نون العظمة بعد إسناده إلى ضميره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the scripture they had wished for, saying that with a reminder from earlier peoples they would be God's sincere servants.
rows.anchor: ما تمنوه بقولهم لو أن عندنا ذكرا من الأولين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the reminder as admonition; Isa's reading بذكراهم supports this interpretation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أن المراد بالذكر الوعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors the Qur'an-as-honor or wished-for-book readings: turning from either is more blameworthy than turning from admonition.
rows.anchor: ورجح القولان الأولان بأن التشنيع عليهما أشد فإن الإعراض عن وعظهم ليس بمثابة إعراضهم عن شرفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi argues that rejecting admonition is also serious because admonition explains how a person's condition can be put right, but calls the contrary objection strained.
rows.anchor: الوعظ فيه بيان ما يصلح به حال من يوعظ فالتشنيع بالإعراض عنه

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر ووهب حيوة والجحدري وابن قطيب وأبو رجاء
rows.claim: These readers use the addressed second-person tāʾ, بل أتيتهم, speaking to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: بل أتيتهم ) بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر ويونس عن أبي عمرو
rows.claim: These readers have بل أتيتهم with first-person singular tāʾ; Ibn Abi Ishaq and Isa also transmit the addressed tāʾ reading, alongside Wuhayb, al-Jahdari, Ibn Qutayb, and Abu Rajaʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق وعيسى بن عمر ويونس عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: In one transmission, Abu Amr reads آتيناهم with a long initial alif; this reading needs no ellipsis of a genitive or figurative construal.
rows.anchor: وأبو عمرو في رواية ( آتيناهم ) بالمد ولا حاجة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: On the majority reading, a genitive may be omitted if the bāʾ means accompaniment; Qatada reads نذكرهم with the first-person plural nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة ( نذكرهم ) بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This links to the preceding أم يقولون به جنة (23:70) and shifts to another rebuke: do they allege that the Prophet seeks payment for delivering the message?
rows.anchor: فهو انتقال إلى توبيخ آخر وغير للخطاب لمناسبته ما بعده وكان المراد أم يزعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خرج means a payment or fee.
rows.anchor: أي جعلا فلأجل ذلك لا يؤمنون بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's provision in this world and reward in the next are better than their fee because they are abundant, lasting, and free from human obligation; this explains the implied denial that the Prophet asks them.
rows.anchor: أي رزقه في الدنيا وثوابه في الآخرة تعليل لنفي السؤال المستفاد من الإنكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord reinforces the argument and honors the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وفي التعرض لعنوان الربوبية مع الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام من تعليل الحكم وتشريفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خرج is anything given out, opposite دخل; خراج commonly means a land tax and suggests greater, recurring obligation. Some distinguish voluntary خرج from obligatory خراج; others say خرج is broader or treat them as synonyms.
rows.anchor: يقال لكل ما تخرجه إلى غيرك والخراج غالب في الضريبة على الأرض ففيه إشعار بالكثرة واللزوم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي والحسن وعيسى
rows.claim: Ibn Amir reads خرجا فخرج; Hamza and al-Kisai read خراجا فخراج by lexical matching; al-Hasan and Isa read خراجا فخرج.
rows.anchor: للمشاكلة وقرأ الحسن وعيسى ( خراجا فخرج ) وكأن اختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using خراج for the Prophet's side may emphasize their entrenched disbelief, while using خرج for God lowers their payment: even a little from God is better than much from them.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى قوة تمكنهم في الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final clause reinforces the superiority of God's provision: the best provider gives better than others.
rows.anchor: تأكيد لخيرية خراجه سبحانه وتعالى فإن من كان خير الرازقين يكون رزقه خيرا من رزق غيره

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i infers that no one equals God in beneficence, while human beings can provide one another.
rows.anchor: واستدل الجبائي بذلك على أنه سبحانه لا يساويه أحد في الأفضال على عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound minds attest that the path is straight, with no crookedness that could justify suspicion.
rows.anchor: تشهد العقول السليمة باستقامته ليس فيه شائبة اعوجاج توجب الاتهام

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gathers the proof: the Prophet was known among them and suited to be chosen; he sought neither false distinction nor worldly payment, called only to Islam, exposed their failure to reflect and blind ancestral loyalty, and they called him mad despite manifest truth and miracles, disliked truth, and rejected the saving reminder. Al-Alusi praises this account.
rows.anchor: ولقد ألزمهم عز وجل الحجة وأزاح عللهم في هذه الآيات بأن الذي أرسل إليهم رجل معروف أمره وحاله مخبور سره وعلنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An implicit يقال لهم introduces the question as rebuke and reminder of why they deserve punishment: God's signs were recited to them in worldly life, and they denied them.
rows.anchor: على إضمار القول أي يقال لهم تعنيفا وتوبيخا وتذكيرا لما به استحقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their wretchedness overcame and mastered them; attributing it to themselves signals that it arose from their own bad disposition.
rows.anchor: أي استولت علينا وملكتنا شقاوتنا التي اقتضاها سوء استعدادنا كما يوميء إلى ذلك إضافتها إلى أنفسهم

rows.speaker: شبل
rows.claim: Shibl reads شقوتنا with fatḥa on the initial shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ شبل في اختياره شقوتنا بفتح الشين

rows.speaker: عبد الله والحسن وقتادة وحمزة والكسائي والمفضل عن عاصم وأبان والزعفراني وابن مقسم
rows.claim: These readers have شقاوتنا with fatḥa on shīn and an alif after qāf.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله واتلحسن وقتادة وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: قتادة والحسن عن خالد بن حوشب
rows.claim: Qatada, and al-Hasan in Khalid ibn Hawshab's transmission, read شقاوتنا with alif and kasra on shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة أيضا والحسن في رواية خالد بن حوشب عنه ( شقاوتنا ) بالألف وكسر الشين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All forms are verbal nouns meaning the opposite of felicity; a group glosses them as the evil end God knew their deeds deserved, a view attributed to most Mu'tazilites.
rows.anchor: وهي في جميع ذلك مصدر ومعناها ضد السعادة وفسرها جماعة بسوء العاقبة التي علم الله تعالى أنهم يستحقونها

rows.speaker: الأشاعرة
rows.claim: The Ashʿarites interpret their wretchedness as the disbelief and sins God had written for them in eternity.
rows.anchor: وعن الأشاعرة أن المراد بها ما كتبه الله تعالى عليهم في الأزل من الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i understands wretchedness metaphorically as desire and pursuit of pleasures, naming the cause by its effect.
rows.anchor: المراد بها الهوى وقضاء اللذات مجازا من باب إطلاق المسبب على السبب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rather than personification as a settled agent, the wording is best treated as a representational metaphor: an affair originating in themselves prevailed over them.
rows.anchor: فنسبة الغلب إليها لاعتبار تشبيهها بمن يتحقق منه ذلك ففي الكلام استعارة مكنية تخييلية

words: غَلَبَتْ عَلَيْنَا شِقْوَتُنَا وَكُنَّا قَوْمًا ضَالِّينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On every account of wretchedness, their words confess that God's proof stood against them: its source was their own condition, so they cannot claim injustice in punishment.
rows.anchor: ومرادهم بذلك على جميع الأقوال في الشقوة الإعتراف بقيام حجة الله تعالى عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were astray from truth and denied the recited signs; their words acknowledge that God does not wrong them in punishment.
rows.anchor: عن الحق مكذبين بما يتلى من الآيات فما تنسب إلى حيف في تعذيبنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects an excuse based on God's foreknowledge or decree: God wrote only what He knew, and knowledge follows what is known, including their poor disposition and resulting choices.
rows.anchor: فإنه سبحانه ما كتب إلا ما علم وما هم عليه في نفس الأمر من سوء الاستعداد المؤدي إلى سوء الاختيار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Satan's footsteps is a metonym for following him and obeying his whispers in every action and omission, including spreading and desiring indecency.
rows.anchor: أي لا تسلكوا مسالكه في كل ما تأتون وما تذرون والكلام كناية عن اتباع الشيطان

rows.speaker: نافع والبزي برواية ابن ربيعة وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the ṭāʾ of خطوات with sukūn; another reading has fatḥa.
rows.anchor: في رواية ابن ربيعة عنه وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر وحمزة ( خطوات ) بسكون الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In both readings, خطوات is the plural of خطوة, the distance between the feet; خطوة with fatḥa on khāʾ is instead the verbal noun of stepping. The plural normally moves the medial vowel to distinguish a noun from an adjective.
rows.anchor: وهو في جميع ذلك جمع خطوة بضم الخاء وسكون الطاء اسم لما بين القدمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the explicit nouns instead of saying ومن يتبعها or من يتبعه intensifies and reinforces the warning.
rows.anchor: وضع الظاهر أن موضع ضميري الخطوات والشيطان حيث لم يقل ومن يتبعها أو من يتبع خطواته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الفحشاء is what is extremely vile; المنكر is what religious law condemns.
rows.anchor: ما ينكره الشرع وضمير إنه للشيطان وقيل للشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in فإنه can refer to Satan or to the matter; one analysis posits an omitted conditional answer supplied by what follows, originally explaining the prohibition. Grammarians object that answers are omitted only after past conditions, citing a line beginning لئن تك قد ضاقت علي بيوتكم; the response is that here the following clause itself stands in the answer's place.
rows.anchor: وضمير إنه للشيطان وقيل للشأن وجواب الشرط مقدر سد ما بعد الفاء مسده

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the pronoun refers to the conditional clause, with no ellipsis: whoever follows Satan becomes a leader in misguidance who commands indecency; this assumes a nominative conditional answer must contain a returning pronoun.
rows.anchor: الضمير عائد على الشرطية ولم يعتبر في الكلام حذفا أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favor includes the clear revealed signs, guidance to repentance that cleanses sins, and the institution of legal penalties that expiate sins other than apostasy according to a group of scholars.
rows.anchor: بما من جملته إنزال هاتيك الآيات البينات والتوفيق للتوبة الممحصة من الذنوب

rows.speaker: جمع
rows.claim: A group holds that legal penalties expiate sins other than apostasy; they answer the earlier Abu Hurayra report by saying it predates revelation of this ruling to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: شرع الحدود المكفر لما عدا الردة منها على ما ذهب إليه جمع وأجابوا عن حديث أبي هريرة

words: مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زكى means becoming purified from the stain of sins.
rows.anchor: أي ما طهر من دنس الذنوب

rows.speaker: روح والأعمش
rows.claim: Ruh and al-Aʿmash read زكى with gemination and imāla.
rows.anchor: وقرأ روح والأعمش ( ما زكى ) بالتشديد والإمالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ungeminated زكى is written with yāʾ despite its wāw root because it can undergo imāla or by analogy with the geminated form, as Abu Hayyan notes.
rows.anchor: المخفف بالياء مع أنه من ذوات الواو وحقها أن تكتب بالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منكم is explanatory; من أحد is extra for emphasis. أحد is nominative as subject in one reading, but accusative as object in the other, with God as its subject.
rows.anchor: و ( أحد ) في حيز الرفع على الفاعلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبدا means ever, without an endpoint.
rows.anchor: أبدا ( لا إلى غاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God purifies whom He chooses by granting grace and mercy, enabling repentance and accepting it, as He did with those involved in the slander who were free of hypocrisy.
rows.anchor: من عباده بإفاضة فضله ورحمته عليه وحمله على التوبة وقبولها منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears all speech, including their expressed repentance, and knows all things, including their intentions.
rows.anchor: مبالغ في سمعه الأقوال التي من جملتها ما أظهروه من التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges sincerity in repentance; repeating the explicit divine name evokes God's divinity as grounds of hearing and knowledge and strengthens the concluding clause.
rows.anchor: وفيه حث لهم على الإخلاص في التوبة وإظهار الاسم الجليل للإيذان باستدعاء الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prepositional phrase في بيوت attaches to يسبح; its repetition as فيها emphasizes and recalls what follows, and fronting signals importance rather than restriction.
rows.anchor: بيسبح وفيها تكرير لذلك جيء به للتأكيد والتذكير بما بعد في الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians call the repeated phrase بدل; al-Mughni calls it emphasis of the preposition by repeating it with an attached pronoun. Al-Alusi objects that explicit wording is stronger and cannot be emphasized by a pronoun; some allow بدل by analogy, and he answers that the whole phrase may be بدل or emphasis with an explicit form to avoid repetition.
rows.anchor: وبعض النحاة أعرب نحو ذلك بدلا كما في شرح التسهيل وفي المغنى هو من توكيد الحرف بإعادة ما دخل عليه مضمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: رجال is the subject of يسبح and follows the circumstantial phrase because its lengthy description would disrupt the verse's smooth order if placed earlier.
rows.anchor: رجال ( الخ استئناف لبيان حال من حصلت لهم الهداية

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani attaches في بيوت to يوقد.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني في بيوت ) متعلق بيوقد

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: Al-Hawfi makes في بيوت an omitted phrase functioning as an adjective of مشكاة; others make it an adjective of مصباح or زجاجة. These analyses restrict the parable to its exemplar and take the tanwin as denoting a kind, not an individual.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي : متعلق بمحذوف وقع صفة لمشكاة وقيل هو صفة لمصباح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi rejects those four attachments as unsuitable: the parable plainly continues through 24:35, and inserting the beneficiaries' state as an aside would improperly interrupt it while opponents' state is central.
rows.anchor: بعد قوله تعالى ( ولو لم تمسسه نار ) على ما هو الحق

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji calls the objection ornate nonsense and says there is no interruption: the parable ends at ولو لم تمسسه نار (24:35). Another view ends it at نور على نور and takes يسبحوا as omitted, with the clause consequential without a فاء.
rows.anchor: وتعقبه الخفاجي بأنه زخرف من القول إذ لا فصل فيه وما قبله إلى هنا من المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed implicit يسبحوا makes the clause follow from the preceding one without a فاء, like قم يدعوك; attachment to يذكر is ruled out because يذكر is governed by أن and cannot govern a preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو بسبحوا أو نحوه محذوفا وتلك الجملة على ما قيل مترتبة على ما قبلها وترك الفاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and Mujahid identify the houses as all mosques.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالبيوت المساجد كلها كما روي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وقتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd restricts the phrase to four mosques built by prophets: the Kaaba by Abraham and Ishmael, Jerusalem by David and Solomon, and Medina and Quba by Muhammad; al-Alusi says this is far from the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: عن ابن زيد أنه قال : إنما هي أربع مساجد يبنهن إلا نبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the houses as Jerusalem, using a plural because it contains distinct locations; al-Alusi also finds this far from the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أن المراد بها بيت المقدس والجمع من حيث أن فيه مواضع يتميز بعضها عن بعض
